title: add-constraint-driven-rag-eval-playground-with-webhook-mocks-and-telemetry
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Introduce a constraint-driven RAG evaluation playground: a lightweight browser-first authoring GUI, webhook mock harness for deterministic tool responses, and telemetry presets for stepwise regression detection. Non-breaking example-level addition intended for developer education and local testing.
description: Motivation: teams need a reproducible, constraint-driven evaluation loop for RAG scenarios that exercises tool-calling and response constraints without hitting live external services. This PR adds an examples playground that combines an authoring GUI, a webhook mock harness, and preconfigured telemetry probes so engineers can iterate prompts, tool bindings, and evaluation constraints locally. What this PR includes: 1) `examples/rag-constraint-playground/` - a compact React authoring UI with live step inspector and constraint editor; 2) `examples/rag-constraint-playground/mock-server/` - webhook mock harness with deterministic scenario fixtures and latency knobs; 3) `examples/rag-constraint-playground/telemetry-presets.yaml` - prebuilt telemetry probes (response time, tool-failure-rate, constraint-violation count) and dev alert thresholds; 4) docs/quickstart.md - single-page quickstart describing authoring flow, local run instructions, and how to wire into Redwood Console for telemetry. Quickstart (short): clone repo; cd examples/rag-constraint-playground; yarn install; yarn run start:dev to launch UI and mock-server concurrently; open http://localhost:3000 and load one of the seeded scenarios; click Run to execute a constrained RAG session; view telemetry in the local console and exported JSON under /artifacts. Constraint model: user-definable assertions evaluated against structured output (must include fields `source_id`, `answer_score`, `tools.called`). The mock harness supports HTTP webhook fixtures and programmable delays via query param `?latency_ms=`. Usage notes: the playground is intentionally lightweight for iterative experimentation, not production; teams should copy the mock harness patterns into their test infra for CI-based regression tests. Rollout plan: merged to examples under `redwood-examples`; will be referenced by an upcoming doc site article (PM-712). Checklist: [x] authoring UI prototype; [x] deterministic webhook harness; [x] telemetry presets and sample alert rules; [x] docs quickstart and screenshots; [x] unit tests for mock fixtures; [x] e2e smoke test in CI. Related: ENG-3245 covers telemetry presets and probe shape, SUP-901 documents a customer request for offline tool simulation. Impact: educational/example content only; does not change runtime nor add new dependencies to core packages.
commits: init: add rag-constraint-playground scaffold and boilerplate
feat(mock): deterministic webhook harness and latency knobs
feat(ui): constraint editor, step inspector, and session runner
docs: quickstart and inline usage notes
test: add fixture unit tests and CI smoke job

Ethan Cole: Approved after small test addition; asked to add smoke CI to prevent regressions when iterating on mock fixtures.
